why: Work participation can support recovery for many people, but timing, duties, risk, symptoms, and workplace support need an individualized plan.

slides.title: Start With the Person and the Job
slides.content: A suitable return depends on your health, job demands, goals, workplace options, and clinical assessment—not a universal timeline.

slides.title: Modifications May Help
slides.content: Temporary changes to duties, hours, pace, equipment, or breaks can support participation when they match the situation.

slides.title: Communicate Clearly
slides.content: When appropriate, agree on current abilities, relevant restrictions, review points, and who needs to know what—while respecting privacy.

slides.title: Pain-Free Is Not Always Required
slides.content: Some people can safely participate before symptoms reach zero; others require more assessment or restriction. Symptoms and function should be interpreted in context.

slides.title: Plan One Useful Conversation
slides.content: Write down one work demand, one current ability, and one possible modification to discuss with your clinician or workplace contact.
